title: Adaptive Cruise Control Strategy for Electric Vehicles Considering Battery Degradation Characteristics
authors: Pan C., Zhang C., Wang J., Liu Q.
model_fidelity: point-mass ACC; Rint battery with OCV(SoC); semi-empirical Q_loss(Ah,C-rate,T); R0 updated from capacity
control_method: AMPC with fuzzy weights vs fixed-weight MPC2, MPC1, PID, SMC
objectives_constraints: safety, tracking, comfort, capacity loss; accel/jerk/gap/SoC bounds; no battery current or power limit
validation: simulation; HIL for real-time timing only
reported_result_and_comparison: abstract: degradation-aware controllers better than traditional ones; 'the fixed-weight controller performs better when following a vehicle at medium and low speeds'; WLTC adapted vs fixed differ in the 4th significant digit (FT)
novelty_implication: Closest analogue: weight adaptation adds little over a good fixed-weight design. Supports R1 direction; removes 'first' claims for degradation-aware weight adaptation

title: Battery-aging-aware co-optimization of adaptive cruise control and hybrid electric vehicle energy management: A constrained hybrid-action reinforcement learning approach
authors: Xu J., Azad N.L., Chen Z., Lin Y.S.
reported_result_and_comparison: not known
novelty_implication: Shows 2026 activity on ageing-aware longitudinal control; HEV, RL; cannot be assessed beyond title

title: A combined trade-off strategy of battery degradation, charge retention, and driveability for electric vehicles
authors: Tawfik M.I., Ali A.M., Asfoor M.Sh.
model_fidelity: battery ageing model integrated in a full vehicle model
control_method: optimal control problem; NSGA-II Pareto over three objectives; online simulation
reported_result_and_comparison: 'prolong the life cycle of the battery and extend the driving range by 25 % and 8 %' with '0.6 %' influence on driveability (baseline not stated in abstract)
novelty_implication: Pre-empts the thesis's Contribution 2 (NSGA-II Pareto of energy/longevity/performance). The thesis cannot claim novelty for an NSGA-II energy-life-drivability trade-off

title: Active Adaptive Battery Aging Management for Electric Vehicles
authors: Corno M., Pozzato G.
model_fidelity: battery ageing model with driver-behaviour Markov model
control_method: online multi-objective optimisation acting on the maximum battery current and the depth of discharge, adaptive to driving style
objectives_constraints: capacity degradation vs range, recharge time and drivability
reported_result_and_comparison: advantages over a trivial strategy and offline benchmark (no number in abstract)
novelty_implication: Prior art for using the battery current limit as an ageing-management lever with drivability constraints. Any P2/P3 'battery-current-limit-aware' contribution must position against it

title: Integrated Battery Lifetime and Energy Efficiency Driving Strategy for Electric Vehicles in Urban Environments
authors: Li B., Zhuang W., Zhang S., Chen M.
model_fidelity: hierarchical; signal phase-time upper layer; spatial-domain MPC lower layer
control_method: hierarchical eco-driving (upper: signal timing; lower: S-MPC)
reported_result_and_comparison: 'maximum improvement of 26.6 % in battery lifetime and 10.5 % in energy savings' vs constant-speed strategies
novelty_implication: Hierarchical urban eco-driving with lifetime + energy is established (the named line). Gains are against constant-speed baselines with trajectory freedom

title: Traffic-Aware Ecological Cruising Control for Connected Electric Vehicle
authors: Li B., Zhuang W., Zhang H., Sun H.
model_fidelity: hierarchical speed planning + rolling-horizon optimisation; stochastic preceding vehicle
reported_result_and_comparison: 'significantly improves the energy efficiency' (no number in abstract)
novelty_implication: Same group/line as LiB2024; battery life as an objective with speed freedom

title: Battery health-aware predictive hierarchical eco-driving control for hybrid electric vehicles via preference-aware coordination
authors: Cai S., Liao J., Huang R., Liu Y.
control_method: predictive hierarchical eco-driving with preference-aware coordination
reported_result_and_comparison: not known
novelty_implication: Shows battery-health-aware hierarchical eco-driving with preferences is active in 2026 (HEV). Narrows any P3 novelty

title: Eco-driving optimal control for electric vehicles with driver preferences
authors: Lot R., Fleming J.M., Chen B., Evangelou S.A.
model_fidelity: realistic EV powertrain; polynomial loss approximation; relaxed regen constraints with braking bias
reported_result_and_comparison: 'energy savings of 21 % with only a 7 % decrease in average speed'; car-following '10–15 % … with no decrease in average speed'
novelty_implication: Named line (eco-driving with driver preferences). Shows double-digit savings come with speed or headway freedom; any P3 must report time

title: Impact of drivetrain regenerative braking assumptions on eco-driving optimal control with driver preferences
authors: Qamar S., Hubbard P., Midgley W., Fleming J.

reported_result_and_comparison: drivetrain-inconsistent regen assumption gives '3 %–11 % higher total energy losses in urban driving and 7 %–12 % in rural'
novelty_implication: Regenerative-limit modelling changes energy results by several percent: unsourced regen limits (as in R1 class C) are a first-order modelling risk

title: Incorporating Driver Preferences Into Eco-Driving Assistance Systems Using Optimal Control
authors: Fleming J.M., Yan X., Lot R.

novelty_implication: Foundation of the driver-preference eco-driving line

reported_result_and_comparison: battery life '+10.33 %' vs baseline (no traffic); ageing −33.02 % vs preceding vehicle
novelty_implication: Speed-trajectory freedom with an ageing objective; not same-cycle tracking

title: Optimal Eco-Driving Control of Autonomous and Electric Trucks in Adaptation to Highway Topography: Energy Minimization and Battery Life Extension

reported_result_and_comparison: energy 'reduced by up to 5.05 %'; battery life 'extended by more than 100 %'
novelty_implication: Ageing benefit computed with the same model class as the optimiser (circularity)

title: Real-data validation of a PSO-optimized eco-driving DNN–MPC for battery-loss-aware energy management in electric vehicles
authors: Djeffal S., Morakchi M.R., Latreche A.
vehicle: generic BEV on a measured VED speed trace
control_method: PSO-tuned DNN-MPC that reshapes speed demand
objectives_constraints: positive battery energy, ohmic loss, speed-tracking acceptability
validation: simulation on a real speed trace (authors state it is not validation of the battery trace)
reported_result_and_comparison: '13.060 % energy saving' and 28.66 % internal-loss reduction vs a tracking baseline; regen −25.16 %
novelty_implication: A 13 % saving obtained by reshaping speed relative to a tracking baseline: the magnitude of the thesis's 12.5 % is typical of trajectory freedom, not of feedback gains

title: Modeling, implementation and experimental verification of eco-driving on a battery-electric heavy-duty vehicle
authors: Heuts Y.J.J., Wouters J.J.F., Hulsebos O., Donkers M.C.F.
reported_result_and_comparison: 7 % to 12 % energy reduction vs driving without EDAS
novelty_implication: Experimental evidence that eco-driving gains are real but come from the speed profile

title: Eco-Driving Strategy Implementation for Ultra-Efficient Lightweight Electric Vehicles in Realistic Driving Scenarios
authors: Stabile P., Ballo F.M., Previati G., Mastinu G.R.M.

title: Analysis of Battery Degradation Effects on Optimized Torque Splitting in Dual-Motor Electric Vehicles
authors: Butcher H.E.
chemistry_cell: not stated; healthy/degraded/late-life cases with capacity and resistance changed
model_fidelity: EDU loss maps + battery electrical model
control_method: offline exhaustive-search torque split (3-D lookup table)
reported_result_and_comparison: optimised split 331.49 vs 337.35 Wh/mi (healthy); 'the range loss caused by capacity fade is larger than the range recovered through torque optimization'
novelty_implication: Independent evidence that ageing-aware allocation recovers only a modest share of ageing losses; also isolates capacity fade vs resistance growth

title: Assessing Impact of Heavily Aged Batteries on Hybrid Electric Vehicle Fuel Economy and Drivability
authors: Anselma P.G., Kollmeyer P.J., Feraco S., Bonfitto A.
chemistry_cell: experimentally aged cells (chemistry not in abstract)
model_fidelity: experimental cell characterisation + DP energy management
reported_result_and_comparison: 'relatively unaffected until the battery loses more than 20 % of original capacity'; at 84 % loss fuel +25 %, 0–100 km/h +3.5 s
novelty_implication: Supports R1: moderate ageing barely affects vehicle-level performance; effects appear when power capability falls

title: Extending the electric vehicle battery first life: Performance beyond the current end of life threshold
authors: Etxandi-Santolaya M., Canals Casals L., Corchero C.
model_fidelity: 2RC electro-thermal with capacity and IR degradation
reported_result_and_comparison: small packs (< 40 kWh) reach end of life through power (minimum-voltage) limits before capacity
novelty_implication: The only route by which SoH would matter for a 4.8 kWh micro-EV pack is power capability; supports P2's mechanism, but NMC not LFP

title: Aging of Lithium-Ion Batteries in Electric Vehicles: Impact of Regenerative Braking
authors: Keil P., Jossen A.
chemistry_cell: high-energy Li-ion cells (chemistry not in abstract)
model_fidelity: experimental cycle and calendar life study
reported_result_and_comparison: 'A higher level of regenerative braking has generally led to reduced battery aging'; long low-current charging, not short high-rate recharge, promotes plating
novelty_implication: Contradicts the thesis's assumed mechanism that moderating charge/discharge peaks slows fade (report.md L3168: 'by moderating peak charge/discharge currents, achieves slower capacity fade'). A fade benefit cannot be inferred from lower peak current

title: Regenerative braking control for electric vehicles with battery and safety constraints
authors: Sun C., Zhang W., Zhu M.
control_method: rule-based, fuzzy, predictive, learning-based regen/brake coordination
objectives_constraints: battery charge acceptance, actuator response, tyre grip
reported_result_and_comparison: 'lower charging current alone does not establish a battery-life benefit'; recommends torque-deficit measures and matched reporting
novelty_implication: Supports P2's framing (charge-acceptance coordination is a control task) and rejects inferring fade from current proxies

title: Effect of Regenerative Braking on Battery Life

title: Regenerative–Frictional Brake Blending in Electric Vehicles Considering Energy Recovery and Dynamic Battery Charging Limit: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach

objectives_constraints: energy recovery under time-varying SoP charge bound
reported_result_and_comparison: recovers 'up to ~98 % of the total braking energy available on WLTP' near the SoP limit
novelty_implication: SoP-limited regen blending is current practice; a P2 layer must use SoP-type limits, and blending alone is not novel
